title: TSMC boosts US investments to $265B on AI boom: report
key_facts: Per Nikkei Asia, Taiwan-based firms have sharply raised investment abroad to supply the AI boom.
TSMC announced an extra $100B capex in July, bringing planned US investment to $265B and four new advanced fabs, 12 US facilities in all.
Quanta Computer approved to spend $973M on server assembly in Tennessee.
Wistron approved to spend $150M on a US circuit-board subsidiary and plans $146M to renovate a Texas plant.
MIC projects the US at 40% of Taiwanese firms' AI server capacity by 2030 versus 23% this year; Taiwan falls to 30% from 47%.
Asia Vital Components spends $245M in Vietnam; Taiwan Union Technology $231.8M in Thailand.
quote_evidence: TSMC leads all the Taiwan players by far.
A recent report from Taiwan's Market Intelligence & Consulting Institute projected that the U.S. would account for 40% of Taiwanese companies' AI server production capacity by 2030.
Taiwan-based companies are building out production capacity in Southeast Asia as well, the report added.
why_it_matters_hint: AI hardware production is spreading to the US and Southeast Asia.
event_date: Nikkei report 6 Oct 2026; TSMC capex July 2026
